questions.text: A can contains a mixture of two liquid A and B in the ratio 3 : 2 when 100 liters of mixture are drawn off and the can is filled with A in the same amount, the ratio of A and B is 17 : 8 and second time when 50 liters of mixture drawn off and the can if filled with B then find the ratio of A and B after second time replacement.
questions.explanation:
Given:

Initial ratio of liquid A and B = 3 ∶ 2

First time replacement of the 100 liters mixture with liquid A

After first time replacement the ratio of liquid A and B = 17 ∶ 8

Second time replacement of the 50 liters mixture with liquid B

Concept used:

The quantity of replacement is divided into initial given ratio.

Calculations:

Let the initial quantity of liquid A and liquid B be 3x and 2x

We can tabulate the data as follows:

  Liquid A (in litres) Liquid B (in litres)
Initially 3x 2x
After removing 100 litres  3x – [(3/5) × 100] = 3x – 60  2x – [(2/5) × 100] = 2x – 40
After adding 100 litres of A 3x – 60 + 100 = 3x + 40 2x – 40

 

Now, it is given that the ratio of liquids A and B after adding 100 litres of A becomes 17 ∶ 8

So, we get:

(3x + 40)/(2x – 40) = 17/8

⇒ x = 100

So, the new quantities of A and B in the mixture are:

A = (3 × 100) + 40 = 340 litres

B = (2 × 100) – 40 = 160 litres

So, we can further tabulate the volume of the two liquids as:

  Liquid A (in litres) Liquid B (in litres)
New quantity 340 160
After removing 50 litres of mixture 340 – [(50/500)× 340] = 306  160 – [(50/500)× 160] = 144
After adding 50 litres of B 306 144 + 50  = 194

 

∴ The ratio of A and B after the final replacement is obtained as:

306/194 = 153 : 97

questions.text: According to an instruction a mixture of colour and Turpentine containing half part of each is perfect for painting a wall. A painter is provided a mixture, 3 parts of which are colour and 5 parts are Turpentine. How much of the mixture drawn off and replaced with colour so that the mixture becomes perfect?
questions.explanation:
Let total amount of the mixture be 1 litre

3 parts of the mixture are colour and 5 parts are Turpentine

⇒ Amount of colour in the mixture = 3/8 litre

⇒ Amount of turpentine in the mixture = 5/8 litre

Let amount of mixture removed by the painter be ‘x’ litre

⇒ Amount of colour in the new mixture = (3/8 – 3x/8 + x) litre

⇒ Amount of turpentine in the new mixture = (5/8 – 5x/8) litre

The mixture will be perfect if, Amount of colour in the new mixture = Amount of turpentine in the new mixture

⇒ 3/8 – 3x/8 + x = 5/8 – 5x/8

⇒ 3 – 3x + 8x = 5 – 5x

⇒ 10x = 2

⇒ x = 1/5

∴ 1/5th part of the mixture should be replaced

questions.text: A trader has two varieties of sugar — Type A costing Rs. x per kg and Type B costing Rs. (x + 12) per kg. He mixes them in the ratio 5 : 3 to form Mixture M₁, and sells the entire mixture at Rs.72 per kg, making a 20% profit on the whole. Find the value of x?
questions.explanation:
Given:

Type A = ₹x/kg

Type B = ₹(x + 12)/kg

Ratio = 5:3

Selling price of mixture = ₹72/kg

Profit = 20%

Formula used:

Cost Price = Selling Price ÷ (1 + Profit%)

Calculations

Average CP of mixture = (5x + 3(x + 12)) ÷ 8

CP of mixture = 72 ÷ 1.2 = ₹60

⇒ (5x + 3(x + 12)) ÷ 8 = 60

⇒ (5x + 3x + 36) ÷ 8 = 60

⇒ (8x + 36) ÷ 8 = 60

⇒ 8x + 36 = 480

⇒ 8x = 444

⇒ x = 55.5

∴ The value of x is ₹55.5

questions.text: A mixture of acid and water has a volume of 164 liters with ratio of acid to water as 21 : 20. What volume of the mixture have to be replaced with 10 liters of water so that the ratio becomes 1 : 4?
questions.explanation:
Given:

Initial quantity of mixture = 164 liters

Acid : Water = 21 : 20

Concept:

When replacing the mixture with water, quantity of acid will only decrease whereas quantity of water will first decrease and then increase.

Calculations:

Initial quantity of acid = 164 × 21/41 = 84 liters

Initial quantity of water = 164 – 84 = 80 liters

Let us assume the volume of mixture that has to be replaced by 10 liters of water = 41x

[Note how we are choosing the values so that we can avoid complicated fractions]

In 41x liters mixture,

Quantity of acid = 21x liters

Quantity of water = 20x liters

∴ Final quantity of acid = (84 – 21x) liters

∴ Final quantity of water = (80 – 20x + 10) liters = (90 - 20x) liters

ATQ,

(84 – 21x)/ (90 - 20x) = ¼

⇒ 336 – 84x = 90 – 20x

⇒ x = 246/64 = 123/32

∴ Quantity of mixture to be replaced = 123/32 × 41 = 157.6 liters

questions.text: A can contain A mixture of two liquids A and B in the ratio 11 ∶ 5. When 16 liters of mixture are drained off and the Can is filled with A in same amount, the ratio of A and B becomes 19 ∶ 5. How many liters of liquid A was contained by the Can initially?
questions.explanation:
Let total quantity of liquid A = 11x

And total quantity of liquid B = 5x

The mixture drained is in the ratio of 11 ∶ 5

So quantity of liquid A drained = \(16\; \times \;\frac{{11}}{{16}} = \;11\)

And quantity of liquid B drained = \(16\; \times \;\frac{5}{{16}} = \;5\)

New ratio = \(\frac{{11x\; - \;11 + 16}}{{5x - 5}} = \;\frac{{11x\; + 5}}{{5x\; - \;5}}\)

According to question ratio is 19 ∶ 5

\(\therefore \;\frac{{11x\; + \;5}}{{5x\; - \;5}} = \;\frac{{19}}{5}\)

⇒ 5 × (11x + 5) = 19 × (5x – 5)

⇒ 55x + 25 = 95x – 95

⇒ 40x = 120

⇒ x = 3

So, total quantity of liquid A = 11 × 3 = 33

∴ 33 liters of liquid A was contained by the Can initially

questions.text: Two mixtures of alcohol and water are prepared by mixing 10 litres of alcohol with 6 litres of water and 8 litres of alcohol with 2 litres of water. In what ratio the respective mixtures are mixed such that the final mixture contains alcohol and water in the ratio 20 ∶ 9?
questions.explanation:
Calculation:

By Alligation method

⇒ (4/5) – (20/29) :  (20/29) – (5/8) 

⇒ 16/145 : 15/232

⇒ 128 : 75

∴ The required ratio is 128 : 75

questions.text: There are two vessels (A and B) contain mixtures of alcohol and water in the ratio are 5 : 2 and 3 : 7 respectively. They are mixed to get a new mixture in which the quantity of alcohol and water are equal, then find the ratio of the quantity of vessels A and B are mixed.
questions.explanation:
GIVEN :

Ratio of quantity of alcohol and water in vessel A = 5 : 2

Ratio of quantity of alcohol and water in new mixture = 1 : 1

 

CONCEPT :

In this type of question, we use the mixture and allegation method.

 

CALCULATION :

Quantity of in vessel A = 5/7

Quantity of vessel B = 3/10

Quantity of alcohol in the mixture = 1/2

Ratio of alcohol and water in which they are mixed

⇒ (5/7 – 1/2) : (1/2 – 3/10) = 3/14 : 1/5

∴ Required ratio in which quantity of vessel A and B are mixed =14 : 15

questions.text: A box contains a total of 100 coins of 1 rupee, 50 p and 25 p denominations. Find the total number of coins of 25 p if there are a total of 49 rupees in the bag and it is known that the number of 25 p coins is \(133\frac{1}{3}\%\) more than the number of 1 rupee coins.
questions.explanation:
Let the number of 1 Rupee coin be 3x.

Number of 25 p coins are \(133\frac{1}{3}\%\) more than 1 rupee coins

⇒ Number of 25 p coins\(= 3x + \left( {133\frac{1}{3}\% \;of\;3x} \right)\)

⇒ Number of 25 p coins = 3x + 4x = 7x

∵ the total number of coins is 100,

Number of 50 p coins = 100 – (3x + 7x) = 100 – 10x

Now, value of 1 rupee coins = Rs. 3x

Value of 25 p coins = 0.25 × 7x = Rs. 1.75x

And, value of 50 p coins = 0.50 × (100 – 10x) = Rs. (50 – 5x)

Total amount = Rs. 49

⇒ 3x + 1.75x + 50 – 5x = 49

⇒ 50 – 0.25x = 49

⇒ x = 4

Hence, total number of 25 p coins = 7x = 7 × 4 = 28

questions.text: A milk vendor purchases 47.6 litres of milk containing milk and water in the ratio 9 : 4. He wants to make this a 11 : 5 mixture of milk and water and sell the entire quantity at the cost price. How much of water needs to be added?
questions.explanation:
Calculation:

The ratio of water in mixture 1 = 4/13 (∵ The ratio of milk and water = 9 : 4)

The ratio of water in pure water = 1

Now these two are mixed to form our mixture 2 where the ratio is 11 : 5

∴ The ratio of water in mixture 2 = 5/16 

Let us apply the principle of the allegation.

⇒ Mixture 1 : water = (1 - 5/16) : (5/16 - 4/13) = 11/16 : 1/208 = 143 : 1

Given that Quantity of mixture 1 = 47.6litre

⇒ 47.6 : ? = 143 : 1

⇒ ? = 47.6/143 = 0.33 litre

∴ The amount of water needed to be added is 0.33 litre

questions.text: A mixture contains three components 'A', 'B' and 'C' in the ratio 5:4:6, respectively. When half of the mixture is removed and with 18 litres of each component is added, the ratio of 'A', 'C' and 'B' becomes 7:8:6, respectively. Find the difference between the initial quantities of 'B' and 'C'.
